question: Under section 19(3) of the Code on Wages, what opportunity must be given before imposing a fine?
expected_conditions: The employee must have an opportunity to show cause against the fine.
source_quote:
No fine shall be imposed on any employee until such employee has been given an
opportunity of showing cause against the fine

question: Under section 19(4) of the Code on Wages, what is the maximum fine for one wage period?
expected_conditions: No more than three per cent of the wages payable for that wage period.
source_quote:
The total amount of fine which may be imposed in any one wage-period on any
employee shall not exceed an amount equal to three per cent. of the wages payable to him in
respect of that wage-period.

question: Under section 19(6) of the Code on Wages, what limits apply to recovery of a fine?
expected_conditions: A fine cannot be recovered by instalments or after ninety days from the day it was imposed.
source_quote:
No fine imposed on any employee shall be recovered from him by instalments or
after the expiry of ninety days from the day on which it was imposed.

question: Under section 6(1) of the Industrial Relations Code, how many Trade Union members can apply for registration?
expected_conditions: Seven or more members may apply, subject to subscribing their names to the rules and complying with the registration provisions.
source_quote:
Any seven or more members of a Trade Union may, by subscribing their names
to the rules of the Trade Union and by otherwise complying with the provisions of this
Code with respect to registration, apply for registration of the Trade Union under this
Code.

question: Under section 6(4) of the Industrial Relations Code, what ongoing membership threshold must a registered workers’ Trade Union meet?
expected_conditions: At least ten per cent of connected workers or one hundred workers, whichever is less, subject to a minimum of seven.
source_quote:
A registered Trade Union of workers shall at all times continue to have not less
than ten per cent. of the workers or one hundred workers, whichever is less, subject to a
minimum of seven, engaged or employed in an industrial establishment or industry with
which it is connected, as its members.

question: How does the Code on Social Security define sickness?
expected_conditions: A condition requiring medical treatment and attendance and necessitating abstention from work on medical grounds.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)
source_quote:
"sickness" means a condition which requires medical treatment and attendance
and necessitates abstention from work on medical ground;

question: How does the Code on Social Security define retirement?
expected_conditions: Termination of an employee’s service otherwise than on superannuation.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)
source_quote:
"retirement" means termination of the service of an employee otherwise than on
superannuation;

question: According to the OSH Code, what is included in the term article for the purposes of the provision on factory articles and substances?
expected_conditions: Plant and machinery are included.
original_title: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (No. 37 of 2020)

question: Under section 26 of the Code on Wages, what is the minimum annual bonus payable to an eligible employee?
expected_conditions: At least 8.33 per cent of the wages earned in the accounting year or one hundred rupees, whichever is higher.

question: Does section 3 of the Code on Wages allow an employer to pay different wages on the ground of gender for the same work?
expected_conditions: No. There shall be no discrimination on the ground of gender in matters related to wages for the same work or work of a similar nature.

question: Under section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, by when must wages be paid to an employee who resigns?
expected_conditions: Within two working days of the resignation (the same applies to removal, dismissal, retrenchment or unemployment due to closure).

question: Under section 70 of the Industrial Relations Code, what retrenchment compensation is a worker entitled to?
expected_conditions: Fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service, or any part of a year in excess of six months.

question: Under section 77 of the Industrial Relations Code, which industrial establishments are covered by the special provisions on lay-off, retrenchment and closure?
expected_conditions: Establishments in which not less than three hundred workers were employed on average per working day in the preceding twelve months (subject to the stated exclusions).

question: Under section 83 of the Industrial Relations Code, what must an employer contribute to the worker re-skilling fund for each retrenched worker?
expected_conditions: An amount equal to fifteen days' wages last drawn by the worker, or such other days as notified.

question: Under section 28 of the Industrial Relations Code, which industrial establishments must prepare standing orders?
expected_conditions: Every industrial establishment in which three hundred or more workers are employed, or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months.

question: Under section 60 of the Code on Social Security, what is the maximum period of maternity benefit, and how much of it may precede the expected delivery?
expected_conditions: Twenty-six weeks, of which not more than eight weeks may precede the date of expected delivery (subject to the stated exceptions, for example from the third child).
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)

question: Under section 114 of the Code on Social Security, what contribution may be levied on aggregators for gig and platform worker social security?
expected_conditions: Between one and two per cent of the annual turnover of the aggregator, not exceeding five per cent of the amount paid or payable by the aggregator to gig and platform workers.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)

question: Under section 25 of the OSH Code, what is the maximum number of hours a worker may be required or allowed to work in a day?
expected_conditions: Not more than eight hours in a day (subject to the provisions on spread-over and overtime).
original_title: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (No. 37 of 2020)

question: Under section 32 of the OSH Code, at what rate does a worker earn annual leave with wages?
expected_conditions: One day for every twenty days of work performed during a calendar year, for a worker who has worked for 180 days or more in that year.
original_title: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (No. 37 of 2020)

question: Under section 43 of the OSH Code, can women be employed before 6 a.m. or after 7 p.m.?
expected_conditions: Yes, with their consent and subject to the conditions on safety, holidays, working hours or other conditions prescribed by the appropriate Government.
original_title: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (No. 37 of 2020)
